# Independent background oracles

Generated by FullProf.2k 8.40 (Feb2026-ILL JRC), executable
`fp2k`, from edi's committed fitting references.
`reference.json` records each source PCR/data/SUM SHA256, generated PCR/BAC SHA256,
original SUM/data SHA256, coefficient values and uncertainties, command and scientific inputs.
No test runs FullProf, fetches a source tree or uses a sibling checkout.

Reproduce with the visible `generate.py`, supplying `--source <edi>/knowledge/fitting/fullprof`,
`--work <persistent-run-directory>` and `--fp2k <executable>`. In a disposable directory it
copies the source data as `oracle.dat`, enables `Ppl=2`, clears **all codewords** and the parameter
count, and runs `printf 'oracle\n\n\n\n' | fp2k`. Count zero alone does not fix the parameters:
FullProf reconstructs its free set from the codewords. All scientific parameter values stay
at the committed PCR values. The saved measured data also bind the CLI observations and sigmas to the source,
including PEARL's converted XYDATA. The saved SUM files remain the source fit's uncertainty oracle.
The completed run logs live in `<author-runs>/fullprof-fixed/<case>/fp2k.log`.

The `Ppl=2` BAC abscissa is the observed abscissa **minus Zero**. Restore the PCR's Zero when
comparing the background with the observed grid. Plain polynomial uses
`u = x / Bkpos - 1` and `sum B_m u**m`, m=0..5 (FullProf manual, Background section,
printed pages 45–46). The 24-term Chebyshev option was added 17 June 2011
(`Docs/FullProf_News_2011.htm`): Nba=-5. Its normalized abscissa is
`z = (2*x - xmin - xmax) / (xmax - xmin)`, where xmin/xmax are the complete pattern endpoints.
The trace and independent closed-form controls demonstrate that normalization, including
interior points. Background dispatch and coefficient AD controls do not infer correctness
from a finite difference of the product.

BAC values come from single-precision FullProf arithmetic and four decimal digits in the
printed coordinates. Absolute bounds in `reference.json` are 0.03 (cecoal), 0.004 (pearl),
and 0.001 (lab6): allowances for coordinate rounding, single-precision polynomial arithmetic,
and the BAC intensity printing. The independent closed-form diagnostic is recorded by
`test_independent_trace_and_closed_form_control`; these bounds are not profile-fit tolerances.
Fit bounds use the source SUM's printed standard uncertainties, separately from BAC rounding.
PEARL statistics belong to the converted XYDATA reference; its vendored PROVENANCE explains
why the original RALF sigma and reported expected R were inconsistent.

`project.py` publishes the declaration seam the gates use: `_background.type` is `chebyshev`,
`polynomial` or prior-art `line-segment`; polynomial declares `_background.origin` (Bkpos);
Chebyshev declares `_background.x_min`/`x_max` (the full-pattern normalization domain);
a coefficient loop declares `_background.order` and `_background.coef` (zero-based order,
parameter free flag in the existing `()` spelling). These are fixture inputs, not a claim
that the current product implements this seam. The loader, saver, calculation and fitting
paths must agree on the chosen declaration. All other model parameters stay fixed; zero
structure scale isolates background mathematics from Bragg-profile agreement.

At kickoff the default crysta neutron table rejects `11B` and `B11` (probe with
`crysta._default_neutron_scattering().length`); `cryspy-compat/neutron.tsv` contains 11B,
6.65 fm. The LaB6 CLI project must declare that source/isotope or an explicit 6.65 fm
scattering-length override, never the natural-B default (5.3 fm).


The CLI coefficient/parameter oracle for CeCoAl is now `cecoal-ls.sum`, copied byte-exact
from the edi project's `fullprof/ls-fit.sum` (SHA256
225ca9d3562af13dcbdec805a9b9b2b0074cfed8502a013a3b432abe372260c5).
FullProf authored it from the same reference with `Iwg 0`; the owner decision is development hub
`c98ab7f36` (2026-10-02). The original `cecoal.sum` (`Iwg 1`, M.L. fit) remains provenance.
Fixed-parameter BAC checks still use the original coefficient vector and unchanged BAC
hashes. `freeze_cli_bounds.py` freezes CLI-only values and standard uncertainties from
the selected SUM, including each background coefficient; no product output sets a bound.
